verdicts.factCheck: Fetched mega-evm v1.7.4 and v1.7.3 crates/mega-evm/src/block/limit.rs and block/executor.rs; both pairs are byte identical (cmp). limit.rs lines 880-890: pre_execution_check returns Err for every candidate once block_state_growth_used is at or above block_state_growth_limit, whatever that candidate would grow. limit.rs lines 387-399 set block_state_growth_limit to rex::BLOCK_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT for Rex through Rex6, and constants.rs at v1.7.4 lines 206 and 211 put both the transaction and the block state growth limit at 1000, so one transaction can fill the block budget. limit.rs lines 819-845 exempt deposits only from the DA size checks, so deposits face the state growth check too; they sit at the start of a block, before any filler. executor.rs lines 585-596 say a rejected transaction leaves executor state untouched and the caller decides what to do, typically put it back in the pool. docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md lines 108-131 say later candidates are skipped and may be reconsidered in a later block, and give no rule for their place in the queue. resource-accounting.md lines 161-187 count state growth per new account and per new storage slot. constants.rs rex lines: SSTORE_SET_STORAGE_GAS_BASE 20,000 times (bucket_capacity / MIN_BUCKET_SIZE - 1), which is zero in a minimum-size bucket, so the cost of about 22.6 million gas for 1,000 new slots is consistent. On-chain, eth_getBlockByNumber latest on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc on 2026-11-24 returned block 32,752,085 with baseFeePerGas 0xf4240 (1,000,000 wei) and gasLimit 10,000,000,000. web3_clientVersion returned mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc. 22.6 million gas at 1,000,000 wei is 0.0000226 ETH, and one per second for a day is 1.95 ETH, as stated. The link that decides whether N fillers delay later arrivals by N blocks is how the closed sequencer requeues skipped transactions. No public source states it, so it is still unconfirmed.
verdicts.codeCheck: The PoolManager code takes no part in the mechanism. src/PoolManager.sol:103-113 (unlock), 143-180 (modifyLiquidity) and 290-296 (take) have no time or block dependence. A delayed transaction runs later with the same checks: NonzeroDeltaCount at line 111, the toInt128 cast at line 293. No balance or delta can be moved by the delay. The effect is liveness only, and it reaches every contract on the chain, not this PoolManager in particular.
verdicts.corrections: The coreRefs mark where victims' calls enter. They are not code that computes anything differently; the hazard sits entirely in the sequencer's admission rule. The unconfirmed queue rule matters only for the amplified version, where N fillers close N blocks. The base effect is confirmed by source: one filler per block closes the rest of that block to every later candidate.

sources.supports: lines 387-399 pick the Rex block state growth limit; lines 880-890 skip every candidate once it is reached; lines 819-845 exempt deposits only from DA checks
TX_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT and BLOCK_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT are both 1000 for Rex; the SSTORE set storage gas scales with bucket capacity and is zero at minimum size
lines 585-596: the caller decides what happens to a rejected transaction, typically it goes back in the pool; byte identical to v1.7.3
lines 108-131: skipped transactions may be reconsidered in a later block, with no ordering rule
lines 161-187: state growth counts new accounts and new storage slots

clearedSpotChecks.check: Monad v0.16.7 touch_memory skips the bounds and expansion check when the same stack element already passed it for at least the same size.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read emitter.cpp at v0.16.7 lines 6276-6311: the cache is taken only for non-literal offsets with touched_memory_size at least read_size, and set_touched_memory_size runs where the full check is emitted. Inside a basic block the emitted order is the execution order, so the check always runs first. The one way a StackElem outlives its block is continue_block (virtual_stack.cpp lines 317-344), and it is used only when keep_stack_in_next_block_ is set. Emitter::jumpi (emitter.cpp lines 3499-3518) sets that only when the fallthrough block is not a jump destination, so the block has the checking block as its single predecessor. fallthrough() (lines 3522-3527) writes the stack and starts a fresh one. new_stack_elem uses placement new (rc_ptr.hpp line 64; virtual_stack.cpp lines 346-361), so every reused object starts at zero. Memory does not shrink within a frame, so a check that passed once stays valid.

clearedSpotChecks.check: eth_call on Monad uses an interpreter-only VM, so eth_call batteries do not reach compiled code.
clearedSpotChecks.note: monad_executor.cpp at v0.16.7 lines 1306-1309 hold vm::VM vm_{vm::VM::InterpreterOnly}, with the stated reason. vm.cpp lines 140-186 run native code when it exists, compile synchronously on a cold cache, and otherwise interpret and compile once the gas bound is reached. The clearance is right. It also means every Monad eth_call result, including this cycle's 185,529 vectors and the pmdiff scripts, tests only the interpreter, and the compiled path rests on reading and models. That limit is stated correctly in the item.
